original_question: For each positive integer e, let A(e) be the supremum of the type t(Gamma) over all almost symmetric numerical semigroups Gamma with embedding dimension edim(Gamma) = e. Here Gamma is almost symmetric if for every integer x not in Gamma, either Frob(Gamma) - x lies in Gamma or both x and Frob(Gamma) - x are pseudo-Frobenius numbers of Gamma. Determine A(e).
target_in_paper: Section 5 (Almost symmetric semigroups), Problem 18: the paper asks for the extremal possible type of an almost symmetric numerical semigroup in fixed embedding dimension. The nearby Problem 19 isolates the weaker finiteness question for the same extremal function.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly focuses on almost symmetric numerical semigroups, fixes the embedding dimension, and asks for the supremal value of the type in that class, which is exactly the content of Section 5, Problem 18. It also uses the same operational characterization of almost symmetry that the paper states in Section 5.
missing_details: The draft should define a numerical semigroup explicitly as a cofinite additive submonoid of N.
It should define the Frobenius number F(Γ) and the set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers PF(Γ); the paper’s type is t(Γ)=|PF(Γ)|.
It should define embedding dimension as the cardinality of the unique minimal generating set of Γ.
To be fully stand-alone, it should say that the supremum is taken in N ∪ {+∞}; the nearby Problem 19 asks precisely whether this supremum is finite for every embedding dimension.
The draft leaves the degenerate embedding-dimension-1 case implicit; for a clean stand-alone formulation it is better to restrict to the nontrivial range e≥2.

For paper-faithful context, it helps to record the small known cases highlighted nearby: almost symmetric semigroups of type 1 are exactly the symmetric ones, Theorem 1 gives the embedding-dimension-3 case, Theorem 13 gives the embedding-dimension-4 case, and Theorem 14 gives a finite upper bound in embedding dimension 5.
No ambient field or ring is needed in the statement itself: this is a purely semigroup-theoretic problem, even though the paper motivates it via semigroup rings.
refined_question: For each integer e≥2, let A(e)=sup{t(Γ) : Γ is an almost symmetric numerical semigroup with edim(Γ)=e}, where a numerical semigroup is a cofinite additive submonoid Γ⊆N, edim(Γ) is the cardinality of its unique minimal generating set, F(Γ)=max(Z\Γ) is its Frobenius number, PF(Γ)={x∈Z\Γ : x+s∈Γ for every s∈Γ\{0}} is its set of pseudo-Frobenius numbers, and t(Γ)=|PF(Γ)|. Here Γ is called almost symmetric if for every x∉Γ, either F(Γ)-x∈Γ or both x and F(Γ)-x belong to PF(Γ). Determine A(e), allowing the possibility that A(e)=+∞.
justification: The draft matches Section 5, Problem 18 of the paper essentially verbatim in mathematical content: the paper’s target is the extremal type of almost symmetric numerical semigroups as a function of embedding dimension. Section 1 supplies the basic notation needed to make the question stand-alone (numerical semigroup, embedding dimension, pseudo-Frobenius numbers, type, Frobenius number). Section 5 gives the definition of almost symmetric semigroup used in the draft, notes that type-1 almost symmetric semigroups are exactly the symmetric ones, and then formulates Problem 18. The immediate nearby context also explains the presently known cases: Theorem 1 covers embedding dimension 3, Theorem 13 gives the exact value in embedding dimension 4, Problem 19 asks whether the extremal function is finite for every embedding dimension, and Theorem 14 proves finiteness in embedding dimension 5 with an explicit bound.
